title: Tools that build models, and models you can change
summary: Thingport now runs small apps of its own — planners, generators and calculators that work with your library, with nine to install and an editor to write your own. A model that came with the script it was generated from can be customized and generated again in your browser, in colour, and multicolour models finally reach your slicer in the colours they were painted in. There's also pairing for Thingport Grab instead of a saved password, five new sites to import from, CGTrader and GrabCAD among them, and a way to find the models whose files have gone missing.

items.title: Tools: small apps that work with your library
items.description: A tool opens in a window of its own from Tools in the sidebar: a planner, a generator, a calculator. Nine come with Thingport — planners for Multiboard, Gridfinity, Skadis and enclosures, generators for QR codes and keyrings, a print cost estimator, a MakerWorld 3MF normalizer and a customizer for OpenSCAD scripts. An admin installs the ones they want under Administration → Tools, with screenshots to look through first, and chooses who may use them: admins only, everyone, or the users they pick. A tool works with your library — it can search your models, read their files, make collections and save what it builds back as a model of your own — and a tool that needs models of its own brings them in a collection of their own, kept once for the whole instance rather than once per person.

items.title: Make your own tool, or ask an AI to write it
items.description: With Users' own tools on, New tool on the Tools page opens an editor: the tool's details, its script as an ES module, the words it shows in each language, its HTML and CSS, and a preview running beside them. It starts from a working tool, Cube maker, that uses most of what a tool can do, and the SDK reference beside it lists the rest. Quicker still, describe one to an AI assistant connected over MCP. A new API token already allows Save a tool, the assistant reads Thingport's own tool guide before it writes anything, and what it saves appears on your Tools page ready to open. Ask again to change it. Use AI on the Tools page shows the steps with example prompts to copy and the connect command ready to paste.
items.code: Make me a Thingport tool that turns a few words into a printable label and saves it to my library.

images.caption: Use AI walks through connecting an assistant, with prompts to copy
The editor starts from a working tool, with the SDK reference beside it

items.title: Change a model and generate it again
items.description: A model that came with the OpenSCAD script it was generated from now leads with Customize rather than Open. It opens the creator's own sliders, choices and text boxes — read out of the script by OpenSCAD itself, grouped as they grouped them — with the model on a stage beside them. Every change can be undone and redone, with the buttons or Ctrl/Cmd+Z, and the script itself is a button away. What comes out downloads as a 3MF or an STL, or saves back into your library as a model of its own with a copy of the script beside it, so it can be changed again in turn. The engine runs in your browser: the script and the values you pick never leave the tab, and there is nothing to install. Models now arrive with their script from every site that publishes one, not just MakerWorld, and a creator who kept theirs back is marked Script not shared so an empty menu isn't left to be misread.

images.caption: Customize takes the main button on a model that came with its script
The creator's own parameters, with what they build beside them
Generative narrows the library to the models that have a script

items.title: Multicolour models, from import through to your slicer
items.description: A model painted in several filaments — a MakerWorld or Bambu Studio project, or one a script coloured — now shows in its own colours in the 3D preview and as its first picture, where it used to draw flat in one. A generated model keeps its colours all the way into the file: a saved 3MF says them twice over, as a colour group that Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer offer to put on filaments, and as per-face painting that Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer and PrusaSlicer apply to filament slots straight away. The mesh stays in one piece either way, so nothing arrives at the plate as open shells. Thumbnails, cards and tag mosaics keep the grey render Thingport tints, so a list of models still reads as one set in whatever colour you picked, and the colour picker steps aside only for the models that brought colours of their own.

images.caption: A painted model drawn in the colours it was painted in

items.title: Pair Thingport Grab instead of typing a password
items.description: Connect in Grab's popup now leads with Pair with Thingport: it opens your instance in a tab to approve this browser and hands back a connection, so no password is ever saved in the extension. Entering credentials is still there under it, for instances too old to pair and anyone who would rather. The popup itself is two columns now, led by a card for the site the tab you're on belongs to — its logo, what that site is, and a tick or an Enable of its own — so the site in front of you takes no searching for. The import panel opens out of its floating icon and shows what you're importing, the model's picture and name read from the page, with one box that searches your collections and creates a new one as you type. On MakerWorld it also says, before you commit, whether the model's generator script comes with it.

images.caption: Pairing opens a tab to approve this browser; no password is saved

items.title: Five new sites: CGTrader, GrabCAD, OwlCAD, Toymakr3D and Makerables
items.description: Thingport now imports from seventeen sites. CGTrader is a marketplace of over three million models with a large 3D printing catalogue: its free models import with your sign-in, and so do your liked models and your wishlist, in one go or synced. A paid one you haven't bought is refused before anything downloads. AWS's bot check stands in front of its downloads, and Thingport gets past it with your browser's token, which Thingport Grab sends, or one FlareSolverr gets for it. GrabCAD is Stratasys's free library of engineers' CAD models, from single parts to whole machines, shared mostly as STEP files a slicer opens as they are. Its files need your sign-in, which lasts two days from its last use: visiting the site now and then keeps it alive, and Grab sends a new one whenever it changes. Anyone's likes import, or sync, not just your own. OwlCAD is a parametric CAD app that runs in the browser and needs no sign-in at all: its library parts convert here, and its CAD projects — which have no file anywhere, only a script OwlCAD's own kernel builds into geometry — are exported by Thingport Grab from an editor tab. Toymakr3D is one designer's articulated robot and mecha models, most of them free, and asks for your sign-in even for those. Makerables is Makera's project site, where desktop CNC and 3D printing meet; its projects and their files import without a sign-in, and only the ones you saved need one. All five are on for everyone under Administration → Providers.

images.caption: The newest five, at the foot of seventeen sites

items.title: Find the models whose files have gone
items.description: Thingport keeps a model's files in its storage folder and only the model's details in the database, so an instance moved without that folder, a backup restored against an empty one, or a folder deleted by accident leaves models with nothing behind them — no pictures, and nothing to open, print or download. A look at your library now finds them and offers two ways out: fetch the files again from the sites the models came from, which keeps their names, tags, collections and favourites exactly as they are, or delete those models for good. Either way the work runs in the background with a bar at the bottom of the app, can be stopped, and ends in a notification. Models only Thingport Grab can fetch are left for its next visit to the site. It's under Repair in the models cog, which checks on demand.

images.caption: What the check found, where those models came from, and the two ways out

items.title: The Multiboard planner draws its own plates
items.description: Installing the planner used to fetch 221 models from Thangs — about twelve gigabytes, as the admin who installed it, spread over several days of a free account's download limit. It now draws every plate itself, as a wall asks for it, so the tool carries only the thirteen joints and needs no Thangs account at all. The board preview is the plates themselves, with the fittings sitting over the holes they drop into and a slider that pulls the wall apart to show which snap bridges what. A finished wall saves into your library as one file per thing to print, with how many to print in each name, or downloads as a zip.

images.caption: The board as the real plates, with the spread slider pulling it apart

items.title: Choose the sites the models list shows
items.description: After Downloads comes a filter button, with a badge counting the filters in force. Behind it: a chip for every site your library holds models from, with its logo and a count, and the Generative switch that used to sit in the toolbar beside the sort tabs, where it read as another sort. What the address keeps is the sites hidden rather than the sites shown, so the first model imported from a site new to your library is listed from the start instead of arriving already filtered out.

items.title: Update a tool from its tile
items.description: Administration → Tools kept a tool's update behind its details dialog. Each installed tile now carries a chip under it: a blue Update where the repository has a newer version, which takes it in one click, or a green ✓ Latest where it hasn't — so the tools that need nothing say so at a glance. An update also takes a tool's models only where this instance already has them, rather than handing gigabytes to an instance that deliberately installed without them.

items.title: Thingport on a phone
items.description: The navigation and the model filters fit a narrow screen. The menu drawer stays inside the visible viewport rather than running on behind the browser's own bar, and scrolling it no longer drags the page underneath along with it. The top bar keeps its search, add, notification and account buttons on one row and drops a long page title to a centred row of its own.

items.title: OpenSCAD runs off the page's own thread, so the window keeps answering while a model is generated — and Cancel is noticed at once rather than after the render it was meant to stop
A wall's plates are drawn several at a time, on as many of your machine's threads as it can spare
Grab's popup says what each site is, not just its name, and counts how many are switched on
A saved wall gets its plan as its picture, rather than a render of whichever plate happened to be first
eufyMake sign-ins work again, now that the site base64-encodes the cookie they live in
Cults3D says plainly when your API key and your browser sign-in belong to different accounts, instead of failing with an internal error — and no longer places a free order on the wrong one
A download that wraps the designer's own archive inside another zip imports its files, on every site
Generator scripts now survive the import from Thingiverse, Printables, MyMiniFactory, Pinshape and MakerOnline, which all dropped them before
A script written on Windows opens with all of its sliders and dropdowns, rather than none of them
A yes/no option in a generator script sets the value you picked, not the opposite one
Changing the sort, the category or a filter while a page of models is still loading no longer replaces the list with the older answer, or leaves scrolling stuck
A model a tool or the customizer made is called generated or created, not uploaded
Installing a tool no longer drops the sign-in from the request and lands on the sign-in form
